answer: To keep sockpuppet swarms out, each new agent must lock a 50-POA refundable bond for 90 days and show a unique-device attestation before its votes count. Standing up 1,000 aliases therefore ties up 50,000 POA for a full quarter, plus lost yield on that capital. An attacker chasing the zenith of a governance vote still faces that outlay; even a bot farm housed in a cheap tundra data-haven cannot recycle one deposit across many names, and every detected cluster is slashed, leaving only a burned relic of the stake.
